newsitem.title: USA: BP plans $20 million U.S. solar equipment plant.
newsitem.headline: BP plans $20 million U.S. solar equipment plant.

text.p: Oil giant British Petroleum Co. Plc will spend $20 million to open its first U.S solar equipment plant in California this year, part of a plan to increase sales in alternative power, company executives said Monday.

BP, which runs 16 solar equipment plants worldwide, wants to expand sales in solar equipment to $1 billion a year from $100 million a year over the next decade, said John Browne, BP's chief executive, during a speech here on global warming.
The plant, to be based in Fairfield, Calif., will make a new type of solar panel using glass-based technnology instead of costlier silicon.
Browne and BP's top solar executive stressed the advanced panels will lower the per megawatt cost of generating electricity, eventually making solar more competitive during high-demand periods.
"This will be something that will be competitive in the future," Browne said.
But Browne acknowleged that solar power, a popular concept during the 1970s oil crisis, will not be commercially viable until technology improves further.
"It is close enough now for us to look at improving the efficiency over a reasonable short space of time to get it competive to peak electricity," he said.
He also said BP plans plans to enter the U.S. power generation market through its solar business but did not specify when or how extensively.
